family_title_en: Identify the predicate of a sentence

stages.ix_title: Identify the predicate of a sentence

what_to_do.en: Tap the part that tells what they do or are.
what_to_do.ko: 무엇을 하거나 어떤지 말하는 부분을 누르세요.

stages.choice_rule: Four unique chunks copied from the stem. One is the full predicate: the action or linking word and every word after it. One is the full subject. One is a leftover phrase from inside the predicate. One is a leftover noun or small word. Every choice word must appear in the stem. Do not add new words. Exactly one choice is the full predicate.

gold_items.stem: The little puppy ran home fast.
The happy kids play in the yard.
My hungry sister drank cold milk at dinner.
<NAME> put the red book on the desk today.
choices: put the red book on the desk today

roots: Copy every choice from the stem. Never invent words, never rewrite, and never add a second verb that is not in the stem.
Offer exactly four choices: the full predicate, the full subject, one leftover phrase from inside the predicate, and one leftover noun or small word.
The full predicate starts at the action or linking word and runs to the end of the stem. Never leave off the last phrase on the correct choice.
Keep leftover-phrase distractors shorter than the full predicate. In tier 3 they must be near misses such as verb plus object without the last phrase.
Use only statements in subject-then-verb order. No questions, no commands, no implied subjects, and no names except <NAME>.
Keep stems in the kid world of school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. No brands.
Exactly one choice is the full predicate. Shuffle its slot across the pool so the answer is not always in the same place.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of four or five words. The predicate is one action word or a linking word plus one word. Distractors are the obvious subject and leftover nouns.
tier_rules.2: Stems of six or seven words with a two-syllable noun. The predicate includes an object or a short phrase. One distractor is that leftover phrase.
tier_rules.3: Stems of eight to ten words. Near-miss distractors drop the last phrase from the predicate or offer only the object. Subjects may hold an adjective.

not_subject.en: That names who or what. The predicate tells what they do or are.
not_subject.ko: 그건 누구 또는 무엇인지를 말해요. 서술어는 무엇을 하거나 어떤지를 말해요.

action_all.en: The predicate is the action and the words that finish it.
action_all.ko: 서술어는 동작과 그 동작을 끝맺는 말들입니다.

linking_all.en: The predicate starts with is, are, or was and tells what someone is.
linking_all.ko: 서술어는 is, are, was로 시작하여 어떤 상태인지를 말합니다.

not_partial.en: Tap every word in the predicate, not just part of it.
not_partial.ko: 서술어의 모든 단어를 누르세요. 일부만 고르면 안 돼요.

leftover_phrase.en: That leftover bit is not the whole predicate. Start from the action word.
leftover_phrase.ko: 그 남은 부분은 서술어 전체가 아니에요. 동작 단어부터 시작하세요.
